title: Technical Writer
description: Learn how to write developer docs, API references, tutorials, release notes, diagrams, and docs-as-code portfolios, mastering modern documentation workflows and tools.

tree.name: Core Writing & Communication Skills
tree.description: Master the fundamental principles of clear, concise, and effective technical communication for diverse audiences, laying the groundwork for all documentation efforts.

children.name: Audience Analysis & Information Architecture
children.description: Identify target audiences, understand their needs, and structure information logically for discoverability and usability. Cover principles of content organization and navigation.

children.name: Clarity, Conciseness & Plain Language
children.description: Apply principles of plain language, active voice, task orientation, consistent terminology, and appropriate tone and voice to ensure easily understandable and actionable content across all documentation.

resources.title: Plain Language Action and Information Network

children.name: Editing, Proofreading & Style Guides
children.description: Develop robust editing and proofreading skills for accuracy, grammar, consistency, and adherence to established style guides. Understand the importance of accessibility and inclusive language.

resources.title: The Chicago Manual of Style Online

children.name: Research & Information Gathering
children.description: Learn effective methods for researching technical topics, interviewing Subject Matter Experts (SMEs), and validating information for accuracy and completeness, crucial for credible documentation.

resources.title: Working with SMEs: A Practical Guide
How to Interview Subject Matter Experts

tree.name: Technical & Developer Fundamentals
tree.description: Acquire foundational technical knowledge to confidently understand, communicate with, and document for developers and technical users, covering core concepts of software development.

children.name: Command Line & Operating System Basics
children.description: Understand fundamental command-line operations (Linux/macOS/Windows PowerShell) and basic operating system concepts relevant to software development and tooling.

children.name: Web & Networking Fundamentals
children.description: Grasp core internet concepts like HTTP/HTTPS, client-server architecture, URLs, and basic web technologies (HTML/CSS/JavaScript concepts) essential for documenting web-based products.

resources.title: How the Web Works: A Primer

children.name: Data Serialization & Configuration Formats
children.description: Understand the structure, syntax, and common use cases for JSON, XML, and YAML in data exchange, configuration files, and API communication.

children.name: Git & Version Control Systems
children.description: Learn Git fundamentals: repositories, commits, branches, merges, pull requests, and collaborative workflows with platforms like GitHub/GitLab, crucial for Docs-as-Code.

resources.title: Git and GitHub for Beginners - Crash Course

children.name: Software Development Lifecycle & Agile Methodologies
children.description: Understand the stages of the Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) and common Agile methodologies (Scrum, Kanban), recognizing the technical writer's role and integration points within these processes.

children.name: API Fundamentals (REST, GraphQL, gRPC)
children.description: Grasp core concepts of different API architectural styles including RESTful services, GraphQL, and an introduction to gRPC, understanding their request/response patterns, authentication, and common use cases.

children.name: API Description Languages (OpenAPI/Swagger, AsyncAPI)
children.description: Learn to read, interpret, and potentially contribute to API specification files like OpenAPI (Swagger) for REST APIs and AsyncAPI for event-driven architectures, understanding their role in generating documentation.

children.name: Basic Programming Concepts (for reading code)
children.description: Acquire fundamental programming concepts such as variables, data types, control flow, functions, and object-oriented principles, enabling the ability to read and understand code examples in documentation.

tree.name: Documentation Types & Frameworks
tree.description: Master the creation of various documentation types, applying structured frameworks for effective content design and delivery that meets user needs.

children.name: Applying the Diátaxis Framework
children.description: Understand and apply the four modes of documentation: Tutorials, How-to guides, Explanations (Concepts), and Reference, to structure comprehensive and user-centric documentation sets.

resources.title: The Grand Unified Theory of Documentation

children.name: Tutorials & How-to Guides
children.description: Design and write effective step-by-step tutorials and actionable how-to guides, including clear prerequisites, verification steps, and basic troubleshooting, focused on task completion.

children.name: Conceptual & Explanatory Documentation
children.description: Create clear and engaging conceptual articles that explain underlying principles, architectures, complex technologies, and reasons 'why' something works, providing foundational understanding.

children.name: Detailed API Reference Documentation
children.description: Develop comprehensive API reference materials covering endpoints, request/response schemas, authentication, examples, error codes, and utilizing generated documentation tools (e.g., Swagger UI, Redoc).

children.name: Release Notes & Changelogs
children.description: Write clear, concise, and user-facing release notes and technical changelogs for new features, bug fixes, and breaking changes, effectively communicating updates to users.

resources.title: How to Write Great Release Notes

children.name: Troubleshooting Guides & FAQs
children.description: Create effective troubleshooting documentation, including common issues, diagnostic steps, potential solutions, and frequently asked questions, to empower users and reduce support load.

children.name: UI Text, Microcopy & Onboarding Documentation
children.description: Craft concise and helpful user interface text, microcopy, and onboarding sequences that guide users effectively within product interfaces, enhancing usability and reducing friction.

tree.name: Docs-as-Code & Modern Tooling
tree.description: Implement modern documentation workflows using version control, static site generators, automation, and advanced tooling for efficient content creation, quality assurance, and delivery.

children.name: Markdown & AsciiDoc for Technical Content
children.description: Master advanced Markdown syntax (e.g., CommonMark, GitHub Flavored Markdown), explore AsciiDoc, and understand the role of reStructuredText for more complex structural requirements, especially in docs-as-code workflows.

children.name: Static Site Generators (SSG) for Docs
children.description: Learn to set up, configure, and publish documentation sites using popular SSGs like Docusaurus, MkDocs, or Hugo, covering navigation, search, versioning, and theme customization.

children.name: Content Reuse & Single Sourcing
children.description: Implement strategies for maximizing content reuse, managing variables, conditional content, and single-sourcing across different documentation outputs to maintain consistency and efficiency.

children.name: Diagramming & Visuals for Documentation
children.description: Create clear and effective diagrams (flowcharts, architecture diagrams, sequence diagrams) using text-based tools like Mermaid, PlantUML, or dedicated diagramming software to enhance understanding.

children.name: Linting, Automation & CI/CD for Docs
children.description: Integrate linters (e.g., Vale, proselint), spell checkers, and automated build/deploy processes (CI/CD) to ensure documentation quality, consistency, and efficient publishing workflows.

resources.title: Automated Docs QA with GitHub Actions

children.name: Docs SEO & Analytics
children.description: Optimize documentation for search engines (SEO) and analyze user behavior using tools like Google Analytics/Search Console to identify popular content, search failures, and areas for improvement.

tree.name: Professional Development & Portfolio
tree.description: Build a strong portfolio, demonstrate advanced technical writing skills through practical projects, and understand career growth paths in technical communication.

children.name: Building a Technical Writing Portfolio
children.description: Curate and present a professional portfolio showcasing diverse technical documentation samples, including project work, open-source contributions, and personal documentation projects.

resources.title: How to Build a Technical Writing Portfolio

children.name: Stakeholder Management & Cross-functional Collaboration
children.description: Develop effective communication, negotiation, and collaboration skills with engineers, product managers, quality assurance, and other stakeholders to gather information, facilitate reviews, manage feedback, and ensure documentation alignment with product goals.

children.name: User Feedback & Usability Testing for Documentation
children.description: Implement methods for collecting and analyzing user feedback, conduct basic usability testing for documentation, and iterate on content based on insights to continuously improve user experience.

resources.title: Gathering User Feedback for Technical Docs

children.name: Capstone Project: End-to-End Developer Docs
children.description: Apply all learned skills to build a complete documentation portal for a simulated or open-source product, including conceptual docs, how-to guides, API reference, diagrams, and a static site with CI/CD integration.

resources.title: Open Source Projects Suitable for Documentation Contributions

children.name: Career Paths & Future Trends
children.description: Explore different career paths within technical communication, including UX writing, content strategy, and information architecture, and stay updated on industry trends and emerging tools.
